title: Oikos common types
description: Primitives shared by every Oikos contract. Contract-wide rule: no floating-point numbers anywhere. Every number is an integer within the IEEE-754 safe range, so Rust, TypeScript and Python all read it exactly and canonical JSON is trivial.

SafeInt.description: Integer exactly representable in every JSON consumer (|n| <= 2^53 - 1).

Cents.description: A balance: an integer in the smallest unit of its account's currency (cents, for a currency with two decimal places), as a decimal string (D58: exact, and beyond JSON's 2^53). Only the outside world's accounts may be negative.

Amount.description: A strictly positive amount of money: an integer in the smallest unit of its account's currency (cents, for a currency with two decimal places), as a decimal string of at most 38 digits (D58: exact, and beyond JSON's 2^53). Its unit is the currency of the account it moves from or to.

Quantity.description: A strictly positive quantity of a resource, in its kind's unit: a decimal-string integer of at most 38 digits, like an amount of money (D58).

Holding.description: How much of a resource is held: a decimal-string integer (0 when it's all gone; an edge's may be negative: goods entering from outside).

Currency.description: A currency's code: ISO 4217 for real ones, or a world's own.

SimTime.description: Simulated seconds since the start of the run; a multiple of clock.tick_seconds once stamped by the kernel. Never wall-clock time.

Duration.description: A span of simulated seconds; the kernel rounds up to whole ticks.

ConfigId.description: Identifier chosen by a researcher in a world config. Lowercase ASCII, no dots, so it can never collide with a kernel-minted id. Unique across all kinds within a world.

KernelId.description: Identifier minted by the kernel: '<prefix>.<counter>'. ent = entity, acc = account, str = structure, rec = record, act = action, msg = message, par = participant, pos = position, cnd = condition (of a body), conn = connection (foundations-2 C3).

LocalRef.description: A name bound earlier in the same action by a block's 'ref' field, e.g. '$trust'.

Basis.description: What an act says it rests on: one record, or a list of records in the order they are cited (at least one, none twice). A list of one is the same as that one record alone, and is stored as it (records: Basis). The kernel checks only that each exists.

RefName.description: Declares a LocalRef; written without the '$'.

Label.description: A vocabulary word defined by the world, not the kernel: an entity kind ('firm', 'bank'), a structure category ('residential'), a kind of space ('dwelling'), a statement kind ('law'), an agreement template ('lease'). The kernel treats labels as opaque, apart from the few reserved ones documented where they are used.

Text.description: Free text (messages, statements, reasoning). Bounded to keep logs sane.

Visibility.description: Who can perceive a record: 'public' (anyone whose channels include it), or only the listed entities' participants (and positions' holders). The author's entity can always see its own records.

Opaque.description: Free-form data the kernel stores and logs but never interprets (claim contents, commitment details, instruction payloads, controller params). Still integer-only: floats are forbidden even here, because they would break canonical hashing across languages. Encode fractions as strings or scaled integers (e.g. rate_bps: 1000).

CellId.description: A cell of ground: 'cell.<x>.<y>'. Derived from coordinates, never chosen.

SpaceId.description: A space inside a structure: '<structure>/<kind>.<n>', numbering each kind from 1 in the structure type's order (apts-3/dwelling.2).

ChannelPath.description: A channel as a participant names it: a personal channel's id, or '<position>/<channel>' for a channel of a position it holds.

Capacity.description: What a participant acts or looks as: 'self' (a person's own), or a position it holds.
